sEn: Qwen2.5-Omni is an end-to-end multimodal model that streams text and speech from diverse inputs, achieving state-of-the-art performance on Omni-Bench and comparable text and speech instruction following.
sZh: Qwen2.5-Omni是一个端到端多模态模型，能够从多种输入中流式生成文本和语音，在Omni-Bench上达到最先进性能，且文本与语音指令遵循能力相当。
absEn: In this report, we present Qwen2.5-Omni, an end-to-end multimodal model designed to perceive diverse modalities, including text, images, audio, and video, while simultaneously generating text and natural speech responses in a streaming manner. To enable the streaming of multimodal information inputs, both audio and visual encoders utilize a block-wise processing approach. To synchronize the timestamps of video inputs with audio, we organize the audio and video sequentially in an interleaved manner and propose a novel position embedding approach, named TMRoPE(Time-aligned Multimodal RoPE). To concurrently generate text and speech while avoiding interference between the two modalities, we propose \textbf{Thinker-Talker} architecture. In this framework, Thinker functions as a large language model tasked with text generation, while Talker is a dual-track autoregressive model that directly utilizes the hidden representations from the Thinker to produce audio tokens as output. Both the Thinker and Talker models are designed to be trained and inferred in an end-to-end manner. For decoding audio tokens in a streaming manner, we introduce a sliding-window DiT that restricts the receptive field, aiming to reduce the initial package delay. Qwen2.5-Omni is comparable with the similarly sized Qwen2.5-VL and outperforms Qwen2-Audio. Furthermore, Qwen2.5-Omni achieves state-of-the-art performance on multimodal benchmarks like Omni-Bench. Notably, Qwen2.5-Omni's performance in end-to-end speech instruction following is comparable to its capabilities with text inputs, as evidenced by benchmarks such as MMLU and GSM8K. As for speech generation, Qwen2.5-Omni's streaming Talker outperforms most existing streaming and non-streaming alternatives in robustness and naturalness.

paras.en: As shown in Figure 2, Qwen2.5-Omni employs a Thinker-Talker architecture. The Thinker functions like a brain, responsible for processing and understanding inputs from text, audio, and video modalities, generating high-level representations and corresponding text. The Talker operates like a human mouth, taking in the high-level representations and text produced by the Thinker in a streaming manner, and outputting discrete tokens of speech fluidly. The Thinker is a Transformer decoder, accompanied by encoders for audio and image that facilitate information extraction. In contrast, the Talker is designed as a dual-track autoregressive Transformer decoder architecture, motivated by Mini-Omni (Xie & Wu, 2024). During both training and inference, the Talker directly receives high-dimensional representations from the Thinker and shares all of the Thinker’s historical context information. Consequently, the entire architecture operates as a cohesive single model, enabling end-to-end training and inference. In the following sections, we first introduce how Qwen2.5-Omni perceives various input signals and present our proposed novel positional encoding algorithm, TMRoPE. Subsequently, the details of text and speech generation are presented. Finally, we highlight the improvements made in the understanding and generation modules to facilitate efficient streaming inference.
paras.zh: 如图 2 所示，Qwen2.5-Omni 采用了 Thinker-Talker 架构。Thinker 类似于大脑，负责处理和理解来自文本、音频和视频多模态的输入，生成高层表示和相应的文本。Talker 则类似于人类的嘴巴，以流式方式接收 Thinker 生成的高层表示和文本，并流畅地输出离散的语音标记。Thinker 是一个 Transformer 解码器，配合音频和图像编码器以促进信息提取。相比之下，Talker 被设计为双轨自回归 Transformer 解码器架构，其灵感来源于 Mini-Omni（Xie & Wu, 2024）。在训练和推理过程中，Talker 直接接收来自 Thinker 的高维表示，并共享 Thinker 的全部历史上下文信息。因此，整个架构作为一个紧密耦合的单一模型运行，支持端到端的训练和推理。在接下来的章节中，我们首先介绍 Qwen2.5-Omni 如何感知各种输入信号，并提出我们提出的新型位置编码算法 TMRoPE。随后，详细介绍文本和语音生成的具体细节。最后，我们强调在理解和生成模块方面所做的改进，以支持高效的流式推理。

paras.en: Text, Audio, Image and Video (w/o Audio). Thinker processes text, audio, images, and video (without the audio track) by converting them into a series of hidden representations for input. For tokenizing text, we use Qwen's tokenizer (Yang et al., 2024a), which applies byte-level byte-pair encoding with a vocabulary comprising 151,643 regular tokens. Regarding audio input and audio from videos, we resample it to a frequency of 16kHz and transform the raw waveform into a 128-channel mel-spectrogram with a window size of 25ms and a hop size of 10ms. We adopt the audio encoder from Qwen2-Audio (Chu et al., 2024b) so that each frame of audio representation roughly corresponds to a 40ms segment of the original audio signal. Furthermore, we employ the vision encoder from Qwen2.5-VL (Bai et al., 2025), which is based on the Vision Transformer (ViT) model with approximately 675 million parameters, enabling it to effectively handle both image and video inputs. The vision encoder employs a mixed training regimen incorporating both image and video data, ensuring proficiency in image understanding and video comprehension. To preserve video information as completely as possible while adapting to the audio sampling rate, we sample the video using a dynamic frame rate. Additionally, for consistency, each image is treated as two identical frames.
paras.zh: 文本、音频、图像和视频（不含音频）。Thinker 通过将文本、音频、图像和视频（不含音轨）转换为一系列隐藏表示作为输入。对于文本的分词，我们使用 Qwen 的分词器（Yang et al., 2024a），它采用字节级字节对编码，词汇表包含 151,643 个常规词元。对于音频输入和视频中的音频，我们将其重采样至 16kHz，并将原始波形转换为 128 通道的梅尔频谱图，窗口大小为 25ms，跳跃大小为 10ms。我们采用 Qwen2-Audio（Chu et al., 2024b）的音频编码器，使每帧音频表示大致对应原始音频信号的 40ms 片段。此外，我们采用 Qwen2.5-VL（Bai et al., 2025）的视觉编码器，该编码器基于视觉 Transformer（ViT）模型，参数约 6.75 亿，能够有效处理图像和视频输入。该视觉编码器采用图像和视频数据的混合训练策略，确保在图像理解和视频理解方面的熟练度。为了在适配音频采样率的同时尽可能完整地保留视频信息，我们采用动态帧率对视频进行采样。另外，为了一致性，每张图像被视为两个相同的帧。

paras.en: Video and TMRoPE. We propose a time-interleaving algorithm for audio and video, along with a novel position encoding approach. As shown in Figure 3, TMRoPE encodes the 3-D positional information of multimodal inputs, which is Multimodal Rotary Position Embedding (M-RoPE) (Bai et al., 2023b) with absolute temporal positions. This is achieved by deconstructing the original rotary embedding into three components: temporal, height, and width. For text inputs, these components utilize identical position IDs, making M-RoPE functionally equivalent to 1D-RoPE. Similarly, for audio inputs, we also use identical position IDs and introduce absolute temporal position encoding, with one temporal ID corresponding to 40ms. When processing images, the temporal IDs of each visual token remain constant, while distinct IDs are assigned to the height and width components based on the token's position in the image. When the input is video with audio, the audio is still encoded with identical position IDs for every 40ms segment, and the video is treated as a series of images with temporal ID increments for each frame, while the height and width components follow the same ID assignment pattern as images. Since the frame rate in video is not fixed, we dynamically adjust the temporal IDs between frames based on the actual time corresponding to each frame to ensure that one temporal ID corresponds to 40ms. In scenarios where the model's input encompasses multiple modalities, position numbering for each modality is initialized by incrementing the maximum position ID of the preceding modality by one. TMRoPE enhances positional information modeling, maximizing the integration of various modalities, enabling Qwen2.5-Omni to simultaneously understand and analyze information from multiple modalities. After incorporating positional information into each modality, we arrange the representations in order. To enable the model to receive both visual and auditory information simultaneously, as shown in Figure 3, we have a special design for video with audio called the time-interleaving method, which segments the representations of video with audio into chunks every 2 seconds according to the actual time. We then arrange the visual representation at the front and the audio representation at the back within each 2-second chunk, interleaving the representations of video with audio.
paras.zh: 视频和 TMRoPE。我们提出了一种音频和视频的时间交织算法，以及一种新颖的位置编码方法。如图 3 所示，TMRoPE 编码多模态输入的三维位置信息，这是带有绝对时间位置的多模态旋转位置嵌入（M-RoPE）（Bai et al., 2023b）。这是通过将原始旋转嵌入分解为三个分量来实现的：时间、高度和宽度。对于文本输入，这些分量使用相同的位置 ID，使得 M-RoPE 在功能上等同于一维 RoPE。类似地，对于音频输入，我们也使用相同的位置 ID，并引入绝对时间位置编码，一个时间 ID 对应 40ms。在处理图像时，每个视觉词元的时间 ID 保持不变，而根据词元在图像中的位置为高度和宽度分量分配不同的 ID。当输入是带音频的视频时，音频仍然以相同的位置 ID 进行编码，每个 40ms 片段使用相同的位置 ID，而视频被视为一系列图像，每帧的时间 ID 递增，高度和宽度分量则遵循与图像相同的 ID 分配模式。由于视频中的帧率不固定，我们根据每帧对应的实际时间动态调整帧间的时间 ID，以确保一个时间 ID 对应 40ms。在模型输入包含多种模态的情况下，每种模态的位置编号从前一模态的最大位置 ID 加一开始初始化。TMRoPE 增强了位置信息建模，最大限度地整合各种模态，使 Qwen2.5-Omni 能够同时理解并分析来自多种模态的信息。在将位置信息融入每种模态之后，我们按顺序排列这些表示。为了使模型能够同时接收视觉和听觉信息，如图 3 所示，我们对带音频的视频进行了特殊设计，称为时间交织方法，该方法根据实际时间将带音频的视频表示按每 2 秒切分为块。然后，在每个 2 秒内，我们将视觉表示放在前面，音频表示放在后面，从而对带音频的视频表示进行交织。

paras.en: Speech. Talker receives both high-level representations and embeddings of the text tokens sampled by Thinker. The integration of high-dimensional representations and discrete sampling tokens is essential in this context. As a streaming algorithm, voice generation must anticipate the content's tone and attitude before the entire text is fully generated. The high-dimensional representations provided by Thinker implicitly convey this information, enabling a more natural streaming generation process. Furthermore, Thinker's representations primarily express semantic similarity in the representational space rather than phonetic similarity. Consequently, even phonetically distinct words may have very similar high-level representations, necessitating the input of sampled discrete tokens to eliminate such uncertainty. We designed an efficient speech codec named qwen-tts-tokenizer. qwen-tts-tokenizer efficiently represents key information of speech and can be decoded to speech streamingly through a causal audio decoder. After receiving the information, Talker starts to autoregressively generate audio tokens and text tokens. The generation of speech does not require word-level and timestamp-level alignment with the text. This significantly simplifies the requirements for training data and the inference process.
paras.zh: 语音。Talker 接收来自 Thinker 采样的文本 token 的高层表示和嵌入。在这种情境下，高维表示与离散采样 token 的集成至关重要。作为一种流式算法，语音生成必须在整个文本完全生成之前预判内容的语气和态度。Thinker 提供的高维表示隐含地传达了这一信息，从而实现了更自然的流式生成过程。此外，Thinker 的表示主要在表示空间中表达语义相似性，而非语音相似性。因此，即使语音上截然不同的词也可能具有非常相似的高层表示，这需要输入采样的离散 token 来消除这种不确定性。我们设计了一种高效的语音编解码器，名为 qwen-tts-tokenizer。qwen-tts-tokenizer 高效地表示语音的关键信息，并可通过因果音频解码器流式解码为语音。接收信息后，Talker 开始自回归生成音频 token 和文本 token。语音的生成不需要与文本进行词级和时间戳级的对齐。这显著简化了训练数据和推理过程的要求。

paras.en: In the context of streaming audio and video interactions, the initial packet latency is a critical indicator of the system's streaming performance. This latency is influenced by several factors: 1) the delay caused by the processing of multimodal information inputs; 2) the latency from the moment the first text input is received until the first voice token is output; 3) the delay in converting the first segment of speech into audio; and 4) the inherent latency of the architecture itself, which is related to model size, computational FLOPs, and other factors. This paper will subsequently discuss the algorithmic and architectural improvements made to reduce these latencies across these four dimensions.
paras.zh: 在流式音频和视频交互的场景中，初始数据包延迟是衡量系统流式性能的关键指标。该延迟受多种因素影响：1）多模态信息输入处理造成的延迟；2）从收到第一个文本输入到输出第一个语音 token 之间的延迟；3）将第一段语音转换为音频的延迟；以及 4）架构本身的固有延迟，这与模型规模、计算 FLOPs 等因素相关。本文将在后续讨论为降低这四个维度的延迟而做出的算法与架构改进。

paras.en: Support Prefilling. Chunked prefill is a mechanism widely used in modern inference frameworks. To support it in modality interaction, we modified the audio and visual encoders to support block-wise attention along the temporal dimension. Specifically, the audio encoder is changed from full attention over the entire audio to performing attention in blocks of 2 seconds each. The vision encoder utilizes flash attention for efficient training and inference with a simple MLP layer that merges adjacent 2×2 tokens into a single token. The patch size is set to 14, which allows images of different resolutions to be packed into a sequence.
paras.zh: 支持预填充（Prefilling）。分块预填充（Chunked prefill）是现代推理框架中广泛使用的一种机制。为了在多模态交互中支持该机制，我们修改了音频和视觉编码器，使其沿时间维度支持分块注意力。具体来说，音频编码器从对整个音频执行全量注意力改为对每 2 秒一个的数据块进行注意力计算。视觉编码器采用 Flash Attention 以实现高效的训练和推理，并使用一个简单的 MLP 层将相邻的 2×2 token 合并为单个 token。patch 大小设置为 14，从而允许将不同分辨率的图像打包成一个序列。

paras.en: Streaming Codec Generation. To facilitate the streaming of audio, especially for extended sequences, we propose a sliding window block attention mechanism that restricts the current token's access to a limited context. Specifically, we utilize a Flow-Matching (Lipman et al.) DiT model. The input code is transformed into a mel-spectrogram using Flow-Matching, followed by a modified BigVGAN (Lee et al.) to reconstruct the generated mel-spectrogram back into the waveform.
paras.zh: 流式编解码器生成。为了支持音频流式处理，尤其是对于长序列，我们提出了一种滑动窗口分块注意力机制，将当前 token 的访问限制在有限的上下文范围内。具体来说，我们使用了一个 Flow-Matching（Lipman 等人）DiT 模型。输入编码先通过 Flow-Matching 转换为 mel 频谱图，然后使用改进的 BigVGAN（Lee 等人）将生成的 mel 频谱图重构回波形。

paras.en: As shown in Figure 4, to generate waveforms from code, we group adjacent codes into blocks and use these for our attention mask. We limit the DiT's receptive field to 4 blocks, including a lookback of 2 blocks and a lookahead of 1 block. During decoding, we generate the mel-spectrum in chunks using Flow Matching, ensuring that each code chunk has access to the necessary contextual blocks. This approach enhances the quality of streaming outputs by maintaining contextual information. We also use this chunk-by-chunk method for BigVGAN's fixed receptive field to facilitate streaming waveform generation.
paras.zh: 如图 4 所示，为了从编码生成波形，我们将相邻的编码分组为块，并用于构建注意力掩码。我们将 DiT 的感受野限制为 4 个块，包括 2 个回看块和 1 个前看块。在解码过程中，我们使用 Flow Matching 分块生成 mel 频谱，确保每个编码块都能访问所需的上下文块。这种方法通过保持上下文信息来提升流式输出的质量。我们还使用这种逐块方法处理 BigVGAN 的固定感受野，以支持流式波形生成。

paras.en: Qwen2.5-Omni consists of three training stages. In the first stage, we lock the LLM parameters and focus exclusively on training the vision encoder and audio encoder, utilizing a vast corpus of audio-text and image-text pairs to enhance semantic understanding within the LLM. In the second stage, we unfreeze all parameters and train with a wider range of multimodal data for more comprehensive learning. In the final stage, we use data with a sequence length of 32k to enhance the model's ability to understand complex long-sequence data. The model is pre-trained on a diverse dataset that includes various types such as image-text, video-text, video-audio, audio-text and text corpus. We replace the hierarchical tags with the natural language prompts following Qwen2-Audio (Chu et al., 2024a), which can improve generalization ability and instruction following ability. During the initial pre-training phase, the LLM component of Qwen2.5-Omni is initialized using the parameters from Qwen2.5 (Yang et al., 2024b), while the vision encoder is the same as Qwen2.5-VL, and the audio encoder is initialized with the Whisper-large-v3 (Radford et al., 2023). The two encoders are trained separately on the fixed LLM, with both initially focusing on training their respective adapters before training the encoders. This foundational training is crucial in equipping the model with a robust understanding of core visual-textual and audio-textual correlations and alignments. The second phase of pre-training marks a significant advancement by incorporating an additional 800 billion tokens of image and video related data, 300 billion tokens of audio related data, and 100 billion tokens of video with audio related data. This phase introduces a larger volume of mixed multimodal data and a wider variety of tasks, which enhances the interaction and deepens the understanding between auditory, visual, and textual information. The inclusion of multimodal, multitask datasets is crucial for developing the model's ability to handle multiple tasks and modalities simultaneously, a vital capability for managing complex real-world datasets. Moreover, pure text data plays an essential role in maintaining and improving language proficiency. To improve training efficiency, we limited the maximum token length to 8192 tokens in the previous stages. Then, we incorporate long audio and long video data and extend the original text, audio, image, and video data to 32,768 tokens for training. Experimental results indicate that our data shows significant improvement in supporting long sequence data.
paras.zh: Qwen2.5-Omni 包含三个训练阶段。第一阶段，我们冻结 LLM 参数，专注于训练视觉编码器和音频编码器，利用大量的音频-文本和图像-文本对来增强 LLM 内部的语义理解。第二阶段，我们解冻所有参数，并使用更广泛的多模态数据进行更全面的训练。最后阶段，我们使用序列长度为 32k 的数据来增强模型理解复杂长序列数据的能力。该模型在一个多样化的数据集上进行预训练，包括图像-文本、视频-文本、视频-音频、音频-文本和文本语料等多种类型。我们按照 Qwen2-Audio (Chu et al., 2024a) 的做法，用自然语言提示替换分层标签，从而提升泛化能力和指令跟随能力。在初始预训练阶段，Qwen2.5-Omni 的 LLM 组件使用 Qwen2.5 (Yang et al., 2024b) 的参数进行初始化，视觉编码器与 Qwen2.5-VL 相同，音频编码器则使用 Whisper-large-v3 (Radford et al., 2023) 初始化。两个编码器分别在冻结的 LLM 上训练，且均先训练各自的适配器，再训练编码器。这一基础训练对模型建立对核心视觉-文本和音频-文本关联与对齐的稳健理解至关重要。预训练的第二阶段引入了额外 8000 亿 token 的图像和视频相关数据、3000 亿 token 的音频相关数据，以及 1000 亿 token 的带音频视频数据，标志着显著的进展。该阶段引入了更大规模的混合多模态数据和更多样化的任务，增强了听觉、视觉和文本信息之间的交互与理解。多模态、多任务数据集的加入对于培养模型同时处理多个任务和模态的能力至关重要，这是处理复杂真实世界数据集的关键能力。此外，纯文本数据在维持和提升语言能力方面也发挥着重要作用。为提高训练效率，我们在前几个阶段将最大 token 长度限制为 8192。随后，我们引入长音频和长视频数据，并将原始文本、音频、图像和视频数据扩展到 32,768 个 token 进行训练。实验结果表明，我们的数据在支持长序列数据方面有显著提升。

paras.en: During the post-training phase, we employ instruction-following data with ChatML (OpenAI, 2022) format for instruction fine-tuning. Our dataset incorporates pure text-based dialogue data, visual-modality conversation data, audio-modality conversation data and mix-modality conversation data.
paras.zh: 在后训练阶段，我们使用带有ChatML（OpenAI, 2022）格式的指令遵循数据进行指令微调。我们的数据集包含纯文本对话数据、视觉模态对话数据、音频模态对话数据和混合模态对话数据。

paras.en: We introduced a three-stage training process for Talker, allowing Qwen2.5-Omni to generate text and speech responses simultaneously. In the first stage, we train Talker to learn context continuation. The second stage utilized DPO (Rafailov et al., 2023) to enhance the stability of speech generation. In the third stage, we applied multi-speaker instruction fine-tuning to improve the naturalness and controllability of the speech responses. During the In-Context Learning (ICL) training phase, in addition to utilizing text supervision similar to that of Thinker, we perform a speech continuation task through next-token prediction, leveraging an extensive dataset of dialogues that incorporate multimodal contexts and spoken responses. Talker learns to establish a monotonic mapping from semantic representation to speech, while also acquiring the ability to express speech with diverse attributes that are contextually appropriate, such as prosody, emotion, and accent. Additionally, we implement timbre disentanglement techniques to prevent the model from associating specific voices with infrequent textual patterns.
paras.zh: 我们为 Talker 引入了三阶段训练流程，使 Qwen2.5-Omni 能够同时生成文本和语音响应。在第一阶段，我们训练 Talker 学习上下文延续。第二阶段利用 DPO（Rafailov 等人，2023）来增强语音生成的稳定性。第三阶段，我们应用多说话人指令微调，以提高语音响应的自然度和可控性。在上下文学习（ICL）训练阶段，除了利用与 Thinker 类似的文本监督外，我们还通过下一个词预测执行语音延续任务，并利用包含多模态上下文和口语响应的大规模对话数据集。Talker 学会建立从语义表征到语音的单调映射，同时获得表达具有上下文适当性的多样化语音属性的能力，如韵律、情感和口音。此外，我们实施了音色解缠技术，以防止模型将特定声音与不常见的文本模式相关联。

paras.en:
We formulate the DPO loss as:

\[ \mathcal{L}_{DPO}(\pi_\theta; \pi_{ref}) = -\mathbb{E}_{(x,y_w,y_l)\sim D} \log \sigma\left( \beta \log \frac{\pi_\theta(y_w|x)}{\pi_{ref}(y_w|x)} - \beta \log \frac{\pi_\theta(y_l|x)}{\pi_{ref}(y_l|x)} \right) \tag{1} \]

To broaden the coverage of speakers and scenarios, the pretraining data inevitably contains label noise and pronunciation errors, leading to model hallucinations. To mitigate this issue, we introduce a reinforcement learning phase to improve the stability of speech generation. Specifically, for each request and response text paired with the reference speech, we build a dataset D with the triplet data (x, y_w, y_l), where x is the input sequence with input text, and y_w and y_l are the good and bad generated speech sequences respectively. We rank these samples based on their reward scores associated with word error rate (WER) and the punctuation pause error rate. Lastly, we performed speaker fine-tuning on the aforementioned base model, enabling Talker to adopt specific voices and improve its naturalness.

DPO 损失定义为：

\[ \mathcal{L}_{DPO}(\pi_\theta; \pi_{ref}) = -\mathbb{E}_{(x,y_w,y_l)\sim D} \log \sigma\left( \beta \log \frac{\pi_\theta(y_w|x)}{\pi_{ref}(y_w|x)} - \beta \log \frac{\pi_\theta(y_l|x)}{\pi_{ref}(y_l|x)} \right) \tag{1} \]

为了扩大说话人和场景的覆盖范围，预训练数据不可避免地包含标签噪声和发音错误，导致模型出现幻觉。为了缓解这一问题，我们引入了强化学习阶段以提高语音生成的稳定性。具体来说，对于每个请求和与参考语音配对的响应文本，我们构建一个包含三元组数据 (x, y_w, y_l) 的数据集 D，其中 x 是包含输入文本的输入序列，y_w 和 y_l 分别是生成的良好和不良语音序列。我们根据与词错误率（WER）和标点停顿错误率相关的奖励分数对这些样本进行排序。最后，我们在上述基础模型上进行了说话人微调，使 Talker 能够采用特定的声音并提高其自然度。

paras.en: We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of Qwen2.5-Omni. The evaluation is divided into two main categories: understanding (X→Text) and speech generation (X→Speech).
paras.zh: 我们对Qwen2.5-Omni进行了全面评估。评估分为两大类：理解（X→Text）和语音生成（X→Speech）。

paras.en: In this section, we evaluate Qwen2.5-Omni’s ability to comprehend various multimodal inputs (text, audio, image, and video) and generate textual responses.
paras.zh: 在本节中，我们评估 Qwen2.5-Omni 理解各种多模态输入（文本、音频、图像和视频）并生成文本响应的能力。

paras.en: Text→Text Our evaluation of Qwen2.5-Omni on text → text primarily focuses on general evaluation, mathematics & science ability, and coding ability. Specifically, we utilize MMLU-Pro (Wang et al., 2024f), MMLU-redux (Gema et al., 2024), and Livebench0803 (White et al., 2024) for general evaluation; GPQA (Rein et al., 2023), GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021), and MATH (Hendrycks et al., 2021b) for mathematics & science; and HumanEval (Chen et al., 2021), MBPP (Austin et al., 2021), MultiPL-E (Cassano et al., 2023), and LiveCodeBench 2305-2409 (Jain et al., 2024) for coding.
paras.zh: 文本→文本 我们对 Qwen2.5-Omni 在文本→文本任务上的评估主要聚焦于通用评估、数学与科学能力以及编码能力。具体来说，我们使用 MMLU-Pro (Wang et al., 2024f)、MMLU-redux (Gema et al., 2024) 和 Livebench0803 (White et al., 2024) 进行通用评估；使用 GPQA (Rein et al., 2023)、GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021) 和 MATH (Hendrycks et al., 2021b) 进行数学与科学评估；使用 HumanEval (Chen et al., 2021)、MBPP (Austin et al., 2021)、MultiPL-E (Cassano et al., 2023) 和 LiveCodeBench 2305-2409 (Jain et al., 2024) 进行编码评估。

paras.en: Audio→Text The evaluation of Qwen2.5-Omni for audio → text includes audio understanding, audio reasoning, and voice-chatting. Specifically, we perform a comprehensive evaluation on Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Speech-to-Text Translation (S2TT), Speech Entity Recognition (SER), Vocal Sound Classification (VSC), and Music, which assesses the performance of Qwen2.5-Omni on a broad range of audio understanding tasks. We utilize MMAU (Sakshi et al., 2024) for audio reasoning tasks, VoiceBench (Chen et al., 2024b), and a self-curated speech-instruction benchmark for voice-chatting tasks.
paras.zh: 音频→文本 对 Qwen2.5-Omni 进行音频→文本的评估包括音频理解、音频推理和语音聊天。具体来说，我们对自动语音识别（ASR）、语音到文本翻译（S2TT）、语音实体识别（SER）、人声分类（VSC）和音乐进行了全面评估，以评估 Qwen2.5-Omni 在广泛音频理解任务上的性能。我们使用 MMAU (Sakshi et al., 2024) 进行音频推理任务，使用 VoiceBench (Chen et al., 2024b) 和一个自建的语音指令基准进行语音聊天任务。

paras.en: Image→Text The evaluation of Qwen2.5-Omni for image → text primarily emphasizes performance in college-level problems, math, general visual question answering, and OCR-related tasks. Specifically, we utilize MMMU (Yue et al., 2023) and MMMU-Pro (Yue et al., 2024) for college-level problem evaluation, and MathVista (Lu et al., 2024b) and MathVision (Wang et al., 2024b) for math. For general visual question answering, we evaluate performance on benchmark datasets such as MMBench-V1.1 (Liu et al., 2023c), MMVet (Yu et al., 2024), MMStar (Chen et al., 2024a), MME (Fu et al., 2023), MuirBench (Wang et al., 2024a), CRPE (Wang et al., 2024d), RealWorldQA (X.AI., 2024), MMERealWorld (Zhang et al., 2024), and MM-MT-Bench (Agrawal et al., 2024). Additionally, we evaluate Qwen2.5-Omni on various OCR benchmarks, such as AI2D (Kembhavi et al., 2016), TextVQA (Singh et al., 2019), DocVQA (Mathew et al., 2021), ChartQA (Masry et al., 2022), and OCRBench_v2 (Fu et al., 2024b). Furthermore, we also evaluate the visual grounding capability of our model on referring expression comprehension benchmarks (Kazemzadeh et al., 2014; Mao et al., 2016), object detection in the wild (Li et al., 2022), and a self-curated point grounding benchmark.
paras.zh: 图像→文本 对 Qwen2.5-Omni 进行图像→文本的评估主要强调在大学水平问题、数学、通用视觉问答和 OCR 相关任务上的表现。具体来说，我们使用 MMMU (Yue et al., 2023) 和 MMMU-Pro (Yue et al., 2024) 评估大学水平问题，使用 MathVista (Lu et al., 2024b) 和 MathVision (Wang et al., 2024b) 评估数学。对于通用视觉问答，我们评估了在 MMBench-V1.1 (Liu et al., 2023c)、MMVet (Yu et al., 2024)、MMStar (Chen et al., 2024a)、MME (Fu et al., 2023)、MuirBench (Wang et al., 2024a)、CRPE (Wang et al., 2024d)、RealWorldQA (X.AI., 2024)、MMERealWorld (Zhang et al., 2024) 和 MM-MT-Bench (Agrawal et al., 2024) 等基准数据集上的性能。此外，我们在各种 OCR 基准上评估 Qwen2.5-Omni，例如 AI2D (Kembhavi et al., 2016)、TextVQA (Singh et al., 2019)、DocVQA (Mathew et al., 2021)、ChartQA (Masry et al., 2022) 和 OCRBench_v2 (Fu et al., 2024b)。此外，我们还评估了我们的模型在指称表达理解基准 (Kazemzadeh et al., 2014; Mao et al., 2016)、野外目标检测 (Li et al., 2022) 和一个自建的点定位基准上的视觉定位能力。

paras.en: In this section, we evaluate Qwen2.5-Omni’s ability to comprehend various multimodal inputs (text, audio, image, and video) and generate textual responses.

Video (without audio) → Text: We assess our model on several representative video understanding tasks, such as Video-MME (Fu et al., 2024a), MVBench (Li et al., 2024a), and EgoSchema (Mangalam et al., 2023).
paras.zh: 视频（无音频）→文本：我们在几个有代表性的视频理解任务上评估我们的模型，如 Video-MME（Fu 等，2024a）、MVBench（Li 等，2024a）和 EgoSchema（Mangalam 等，2023）。

paras.en: Multimodality → Text: We demonstrate our model's ability to handle mixed-modality (image, audio, and text) prompts on OmniBench (Li et al., 2024b).
paras.zh: 多模态→文本：我们在 OmniBench（Li 等，2024b）上展示了模型处理混合模态（图像、音频和文本）提示的能力。

paras.en: 5.1.1 Performance of Text→Text. We compare Qwen2.5-Omni with other leading large language models of similar size (7B). As shown in Table 1, the performance of Qwen2.5-Omni generally falls between Qwen2-7B and Qwen2.5-7B. Our model outperforms Qwen2-7B on most benchmarks, such as MMLU-Pro, MMLU-redux, MATH, GSM8K, MBPP, MultiPL-E, and LiveCodeBench, which demonstrates the exceptional capabilities of our model for Text→Text. Table 1: Text → Text performance of 7B+ pure text models and Qwen2.5-Omni.
paras.zh: 5.1.1 文本→文本性能。我们将 Qwen2.5-Omni 与相近规模（7B）的其他领先大语言模型进行比较。如表 1 所示，Qwen2.5-Omni 的性能总体介于 Qwen2-7B 和 Qwen2.5-7B 之间。我们的模型在大多数基准测试上优于 Qwen2-7B，如 MMLU-Pro、MMLU-redux、MATH、GSM8K、MBPP、MultiPL-E 和 LiveCodeBench，这展示了我们模型在文本→文本方面的卓越能力。表 1：7B+ 纯文本模型与 Qwen2.5-Omni 的文本→文本性能。

paras.en: 5.1.2 Performance of Audio→Text. We compare Qwen2.5-Omni with other leading specialist or generalist models on diverse audio understanding, audio reasoning, and voice-chatting benchmarks. As shown in Tables 2 and 3, Qwen2.5-Omni delivers better or comparable performance with other state-of-the-art methods on audio understanding. For instance, it achieves superior ASR and S2TT performance on Fleurs_zh, CommonVoice_en, CommonVoice_zh, CoVoST2_en-de, and CoVoST2_zh-en test sets, surpassing previous state-of-the-art models like Whisper-large-v3, Qwen2-Audio, MinMo, and other Omni models. Qwen2.5-Omni also achieves state-of-the-art performance on general audio understanding tasks like music and VSC. Additionally, Qwen2.5-Omni achieves state-of-the-art results on audio reasoning with superior performance on sound, music, and speech subsets of the MMAU benchmark. These results demonstrate the powerful capabilities of Qwen2.5-Omni in general audio understanding and reasoning. Furthermore, on VoiceBench, Qwen2.5-Omni achieves an impressive average score of 74.12, surpassing other audio language models and Omni models of similar size. This showcases our model's strong capabilities in speech interaction. To further explore the performance of diverse speech interaction, we convert text instructions from several pure-text benchmarks into speech and evaluate Qwen2.5-Omni, Qwen2-Audio, and Qwen2-7B on an in-house voice-chat benchmark. About 90% of text instructions are utilized. We use speech instructions for Qwen2.5-Omni and Qwen2-Audio, and text instructions for Qwen2-7B. As shown in Table 4, compared to Qwen2-Audio, Qwen2.5-Omni significantly narrows the gap with Qwen2-7B, which uses text instructions. This reflects our model's substantial progress in diversified end-to-end speech interaction.
paras.zh: 5.1.2 音频→文本性能。我们将 Qwen2.5-Omni 与其他领先的专项或通用模型在多种音频理解、音频推理和语音对话基准上进行比较。如表 2 和表 3 所示，Qwen2.5-Omni 在音频理解方面与其他最先进方法相比表现更好或相当。例如，它在 Fleurs_zh、CommonVoice_en、CommonVoice_zh、CoVoST2_en-de 和 CoVoST2_zh-en 测试集上取得了优越的 ASR 和 S2TT 性能，超过了之前的先进模型，如 Whisper-large-v3、Qwen2-Audio、MinMo 和其他 Omni 模型。Qwen2.5-Omni 还在音乐和 VSC 等一般音频理解任务上达到了最先进的性能。此外，Qwen2.5-Omni 在音频推理方面取得了最先进的结果，在 MMAU 基准的声音、音乐和语音子集上表现出优越性能。这些结果证明了 Qwen2.5-Omni 在一般音频理解和推理方面的强大能力。此外，在 VoiceBench 上，Qwen2.5-Omni 取得了令人印象深刻的平均分 74.12，超过了相近规模的其他音频语言模型和 Omni 模型。这展示了我们模型在语音交互方面的强大能力。为了进一步探索多样化语音交互的性能，我们将几个纯文本基准测试中的文本指令转换为语音，并在内部语音对话基准上评估 Qwen2.5-Omni、Qwen2-Audio 和 Qwen2-7B。我们使用了大约 90% 的文本指令。我们对 Qwen2.5-Omni 和 Qwen2-Audio 使用语音指令，对 Qwen2-7B 使用文本指令。如表 4 所示，与 Qwen2-Audio 相比，Qwen2.5-Omni 显著缩小了与使用文本指令的 Qwen2-7B 之间的差距。这反映了我们模型在多样化端到端语音交互方面的实质性进展。

paras.en: In this section, we evaluate the speech generation capabilities of Qwen2.5-Omni. Due to the lack of relevant assessments, the evaluation of speech generation focuses primarily on speech generation given text, similar to text-to-speech (TTS), across two aspects: zero-shot and single-speaker speech generation capabilities.
paras.zh: 在本节中，我们评估 Qwen2.5-Omni 的语音生成能力。由于缺乏相关的评估标准，语音生成的评估主要关注给定文本的语音生成，类似于文本到语音（TTS），涵盖两个方面：零样本和单说话人语音生成能力。

paras.en: • Zero-Shot Speech Generation: We assessed the content consistency (WER) and speaker similarity (SIM) of our model in zero-shot speech generation on SEED (Anastassiou et al., 2024). • Single-Speaker Speech Generation: We assessed the stability of our speaker fine-tuned model on SEED (Anastassiou et al., 2024), and evaluated the subjective naturalness (NMOS) of the generated speech on a self-created dataset.
paras.zh: • 零样本语音生成：我们在 SEED 数据集（Anastassiou et al., 2024）上评估了模型在零样本语音生成中的内容一致性（WER）和说话人相似度（SIM）。• 单说话人语音生成：我们在 SEED 数据集（Anastassiou et al., 2024）上评估了经过说话人微调后的模型的稳定性，并在自建数据集上评估了生成语音的主观自然度（NMOS）。

paras.en: 5.2.1 Evaluation of Zero-Shot Speech Generation. We compared the Qwen2.5-Omni with state-of-the-art zero-shot TTS systems. As shown in Table 9, Qwen2.5-Omni demonstrates highly competitive performance, highlighting its robust speech understanding and generation capabilities developed through in-context learning (ICL). Additionally, after reinforcement learning (RL) optimization, Qwen2.5-Omni showed significant improvements in generation stability, with marked reductions in attention misalignment, pronunciation errors, and inappropriate pauses on the challenging test-hard dataset.
paras.zh: 5.2.1 零样本语音生成评估。我们将 Qwen2.5-Omni 与最先进的零样本 TTS 系统进行了比较。如表 9 所示，Qwen2.5-Omni 表现出极具竞争力的性能，突显了其通过上下文学习（ICL）发展出的强大的语音理解和生成能力。此外，经过强化学习（RL）优化后，Qwen2.5-Omni 在生成稳定性方面取得了显著提升，在具有挑战性的 test-hard 数据集上，注意力错位、发音错误和不恰当停顿均大幅减少。

paras.en: 5.2.2 Evaluation of Single-Speaker Speech Generation. We compared the Qwen2.5-Omni model before and after speaker fine-tuning, as well as with human recordings. As shown in Table 10, the speaker-finetuned Qwen2.5-Omni more precisely captured the nuanced prosodic styles of the target speakers while preserving the foundational stability provided by the base model, achieving performance that approaches human-level quality across both subjective and objective metrics.
paras.zh: 5.2.2 单说话人语音生成评估。我们比较了 Qwen2.5-Omni 在说话人微调前后的模型，以及人工录音。如表 10 所示，经过说话人微调的 Qwen2.5-Omni 更精确地捕捉了目标说话人的细微韵律风格，同时保持了基础模型提供的稳定性，在主观和客观指标上均达到了接近人类水平的表现。

paras.en: Qwen2.5-Omni is a unified model designed to understand and generate multiple modalities, including text and real-time speech. To enhance video integration, we’ve introduced a new positional embedding method called TMRoPE, which aligns audio and video timing. Our Thinker-Talker framework supports real-time speech generation while minimizing interference across different modalities. Additionally, we employ techniques such as block-wise audio/vision encoding and a sliding window mechanism for codeto-wav generation. This innovative model excels in complex audio-visual interactions and emotional

Comprehensive evaluations show that Qwen2.5-Omni outperforms similarly sized single-modality models, particularly in following voice commands, and achieves state-of-the-art performance in multi-modal tasks. In the development of the model, we have identified several critical issues that have often been overlooked by researchers in previous academic studies, such as video OCR and audio-video collaborative understanding. Addressing these challenges necessitates collaboration between the academic and industrial sectors, particularly in building comprehensive evaluation benchmarks and research datasets. We believe Qwen2.5-Omni represents a significant advancement toward artificial general intelligence (AGI). Our future goals include developing a more robust and faster model with expanded output capabilities across various modalities like images, videos, and music.
